newsitem.title: UK: Japanese shares nudge lower in London trading.
newsitem.headline: Japanese shares nudge lower in London trading.

text.p: Japanese stocks weakened in London trading on Monday, extending their losses in Tokyo and little affected by comments from the Bank of Japan that the country's economic recovery was becoming more solid, dealers said.
With Wall Street adding to Friday's 148-point tumble in London trading hours, dealers said Japan would likely take its lead from the Dow close at Tuesday's start in Tokyo.
"If anything shares are a bit weaker but it is all subject to what the U.S. does later today," said a dealer at one leading Japanese brokerage in London.

The Nikkei 50 index of stocks in London was down 14.43 points or one percent from Friday's London close at 1,427.97, representing a slight extension of Monday's drop in the Nikkei 225, which closed 154.51 points or 0.9 percent lower at 17,692.47.
Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita said Japan's recovery would continue after a temporary slowdown caused by a rise in sales tax this month.
Meantime Merrill Lynch said on Monday a survey of UK fund managers found they were becoming more optimistic on the outlook for Japanese shares.

The poll, which took the views of 72 institutions managing funds of $1,550 billion between April 7 and 9, found that a balance of 21 percent planned to increase their holdings of UK shares, up from 18 percent the month before.
